idiom_name: AsyncChannel / AsyncThrowingChannel as the error channel plus a dedicated error topic on the broker client
implementation_notes: Swift ships a first-class channel primitive but no messaging framework: AsyncChannel and AsyncThrowingChannel from swift-async-algorithms are reference-type async sequences with back pressure - send(_:) suspends until the consumer iterates - so they are the natural invalid-message channel inside a process. The decoder task sends the raw element plus a reason into the error channel instead of failing the shared stream, and for broker-backed systems the same structure maps to a second topic or queue handled by a NIO-based client, with the same rule: the raw frame travels, never a partially decoded value. Topology and the routing decision stay application code, which is why the support level is manual rather than library.
pitfalls: Calling errors.fail(_:) terminates the channel for every consumer; one bad element must be sent, not thrown into the shared channel.
send(_:) suspends until the error consumer iterates, so a stalled error handler applies back pressure to the whole pipeline - relay through a buffered channel if the error path can be slow.
Elements crossing task boundaries must be Sendable; a decoded struct holding non-Sendable references cannot be forwarded and forces a raw-bytes payload.
